Subject: Acme Health — private deployment security Q&A and next steps

Hi Julia / Michael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on requirements and decision criteria for the private deployment options (VPC-hosted private control plane vs fully on-prem / air-gapped):

Summary from our side:
- Primary requirement: PHI-processing workloads (HIPAA) for a subset of endpoints; low-latency inference for clinician workflows.
- Data residency: US-only, strict egress restrictions.
- Preference: private control plane in your VPC or air-gapped on-prem if required by compliance.
- Non-negotiables: KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys, audit logs for all inference requests, and SOC 2 Type II evidence.

Open items we raised on the call (please confirm):
1) SOC 2 status and any gap dates (Type II report availability).
2) HIPAA BA agreement timing and contract owner at Acme.
3) Whether your infra team requires a fully air-gapped deployment or if a VPC private control plane with no public egress is acceptable.
4) A current network diagram (subnets, NAT/bastion, egress restrictions) and the list of allowed outbound endpoints/ports.

Attached I’ve included the Acme_VPC_Requirements_20260210.pdf that summarizes the items we discussed and the Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx as a starter the Redwood security team can fill out (we’ll populate the first pass and send back).

Next steps I propose:
- Acme to confirm SOC 2 / HIPAA timelines and send a network diagram (Michael or infra).
- Redwood (Dev + Laura) to complete first pass of vendor questionnaire and return by EOD Thursday (2026-02-12).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Acme infra for Thursday 2026-02-12 11:00 AM PT to walk deployment diagram and port requirements.

If that timeline works I’ll send the calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sergio

Thanks, Sergio — great summary. A few quick answers from our side:

- SOC 2: Acme Health has a SOC 2 Type II in place for our core platform, but third-party vendors are required to provide either a SOC 2 report or an SOC 2 bridge letter. We do not have Redwood’s Type II yet — can you share current compliance docs or a SOC 2 attestation timeline?
- HIPAA / BA: We need Redwood to sign a BA. Procurement is cc’ed here — procurement@acmehealth.com is the owner for contracting.
- Air-gapped vs VPC: Our default is VPC private control plane (no internet egress). Air-gapped on-prem will be considered only if the control plane cannot be made fully private. Michael will share the infra diagram and a list of approved outbound endpoints.

Michael, can you share the network diagram and the contact for our compliance team?

We’ll look out for your filled questionnaire. Thursday at 11 AM PT works for us.

Regards,
Julia Park
Director, IT Security, Acme Health
julia.park@acmehealth.com

Sergio / Julia — attaching the requested diagram in this reply. A few technical clarifications from infra: 

- Our preferred setup: single-tenant private control plane in our AWS account. No public internet egress for inference nodes; egress allowed only to our internal monitoring endpoints and to S3 (with VPC endpoint).
- Required ports: outbound TCP 443 only, and a limited set of outbound DNS; we block all other outbound traffic.
- Authentication: we require support for external KMS through AWS KMS and an option for HSM-backed keys.
- Audit logs: we need request-level logs forwarded to our centralized SIEM (via secure forwarder).
- Air-gap option: if you can’t support private-control-plane egress constraints and on-prem KMS/HSM, we will explore air-gapped deployment, but that adds procurement and ops overhead.

Attached: deployment_diagram_acme_v2.png

-Michael

Thanks for the diagram Michael — helpful. A few technical notes from Redwood infra and some questions so we prepare the questionnaire answers correctly:

1) Private control plane: we can deploy a customer-dedicated control plane inside your AWS account (CloudFormation + operator). This runs without public internet egress if you route AWS API endpoints via VPC endpoints and restrict NAT. Is your team able to allow the following AWS endpoints via VPC endpoints: sts, s3, kms, cloudwatch logs?

2) KMS/HSM: we support external KMS through an API integration pattern; we also offer an optional on-host HSM-backed key provider for fully isolated key material. Which approach is preferred? If HSM, we’ll need the procurement lead to sign off on HSM logistics.

3) SIEM/log forwarding: Redwood can stream audit logs to your SIEM via a secure forwarder (mutual TLS). We’ll include the configuration in the questionnaire. Are there any SIEM ingestion limits we should be aware of?

4) Air-gap variant: our on-prem package requires physical connectivity for initial image + license provisioning. If Acme needs completely offline runtime with no outbound at all, that’s possible but expects a 6–8 week ops lead time and separate contract terms.

We’ll fill out the Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx and return a completed draft by EOD today (Thursday). Attaching the completed workbook and a short runbook for private control plane setup once we finish.

Thanks,
